name: New York City
note: aerial-photograph ground (no open LiDAR over the built-up city: bare-earth LiDAR erases the streets); the street grid, the 1865 shoreline, the squares and church footprints carry the fit; the 1811 and 1865 sheets span the island beyond the 2000 m town box, so those fits are likely to end review items (the Venice precedent, docs/lead_artists.md)

name: Washington, D.C.
note: aerial-photograph ground (no open LiDAR over the built-up city: bare-earth LiDAR erases the streets); the street grid, the diagonal avenues, the Potomac shoreline and the squares carry the fit; the 1865 defences ring spans ~35 km beyond the 2000 m town box, so that fit is likely to end a review item (the Venice precedent, docs/lead_artists.md); the ring's forts are candidate kind-'fort' sites and the catalog already has the individuals (Fort Bayard Q3077774, Fort DeRussy Q5471024, Fort Totten Q18150335, Fort Marcy Q61784495, Fort Foote Q14691922, all part_of Q5124610 'Civil War defenses of Washington, D.C.' - data/catalog/sites.jsonl)

name: San Francisco
note: aerial-photograph ground (no open LiDAR over the built-up city: bare-earth LiDAR erases the streets); the street grid, the bay shoreline (the 1854 sheet's red water-front line), the squares and the hills carry the fit; the 1849/1850 sheets draw the old peninsula tip to tip in the 2000 m town box (~30 m overshoot at each drawn tip); the point is the midpoint of the two drawn tips (Washington & Jones / Rincon Point), not a P625 (see the SITES comment); the 1854 sheet's 1850s growth (the Center Street grid, the Market & 10th-11th corner) reaches past the box's SW corner - likely a review item (the NY 1811 precedent, docs/lead_artists.md)

name: Nashville
note: aerial-photograph ground (no open LiDAR over the built-up city: bare-earth LiDAR erases the streets); the street grid, the Cumberland shoreline, the squares and the church footprints carry the fit; the point is the center of the projected 1804 drawn extent (the 147/148 SF precedent) - P625 is 721 m NE and its 2000 m box overshoots the drawn extent W 543 m, so it is not a P625; the 1804 Clayton plan is a near north-up bird's-eye view (~6 deg tilt, 0.852 m/px); the other three staged sheets span beyond the 2000 m town box, so their fits are likely to end review items (the NY 1811 / DC 1865 ring precedent); Fort Negley Q5471744 (drawn on the 1895 plate) gets a fort site of its own (1600 m box, a 3DEP LiDAR candidate) only when a fort-only plan is found - none is on Commons (the 3 Fletcher 1864 views are 236b leads)
